correctness.rationale: For every even N≥4 the kernel of R is the span of even/odd checkerboard vectors and im R is its orthogonal complement; a 2×2 incidence Gram matrix B with entries q and q+m (mod 2) gives dim ker T∩im T=2−rank B, hence rank T²=N−4+rank B. Its determinant is 1 for N≡2 (mod 4), otherwise its rank equals q∈{0,1}. Equality of first and second image implies every first-image state is periodic, with exact cardinalities and four-to-one predecessor counting. The nilpotent Jordan-block count follows from the intersection. Exact 49,660 finite matrix-permutation checks replayed, supplementary only; proof covers all permutations/dimensions.

value.rationale: A sharp universal dichotomy over all N! site permutations quantifies whether a discrete XOR ring has an immediately periodic core, giving exact periodic versus direct-transient populations at N≡2 mod 4. For N divisible by four, an exact parity-incidence classification gives the initial nilpotent Jordan-chain multiplicity and exact second-image size, with explicit prefix-shift consequences. The motivating 2026 paper highlights the factorial wiring difficulty and stability of direct periodic orbits yet excludes even N; this resolves a natural structural gap beyond a routine single-instance computation.
